T1. Historical report [NO]

Synopsis:
Global sovereign bond yields are surging, driven by rising real (inflation-adjusted) rates rather than inflation expectations. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signaled at Jackson Hole that US monetary policy is not restrictive, financial conditions remain loose, and the Fed has "work to do." Markets have repriced sharply: ~70% probability of a September hike, two full hikes priced by March 2027, and the policy rate never falling below 4% through 2028. The structural driver is the AI-fueled capex boom lifting global demand for capital, forcing central banks worldwide to reassess where the neutral rate ("R-star") actually sits — likely higher than current official estimates.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES — The US is the central anchor of the piece, with global bond moves contextualized around Fed policy and the neutral rate reassessment.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 90 (strongly YES)
Probability of increase: 70% (near-term September hike per fed futures cited in article; further hikes beyond that are also priced)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 10 (effectively NO)
Probability of holding: 30%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (NO — cuts are explicitly ruled out through 2028 in the futures strip)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 80 (Decidedly more hawkish — Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks explicitly rejected the "restrictive" characterization, futures re-priced sharply toward multiple hikes, real rates rising fast, and the neutral rate itself is being revised upward structurally)
